title: The Billie Holiday date with Benny Goodman and Freddie Green joining
summary: He recalls a January 1937 Billie Holiday recording with Goodman, Teddy Wilson and the Basie men, after which Freddie Green joined the band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: If we did anything when we was at the Roseland for a month - if there was anything that he played that month, I would have to try to find some old dir shots that was made in 1936 coming into the first 2 weeks of January, because 'round about January the 17th or 18th we made a recording with Benny Goodman, Billie Holiday, Teddy Wilson,
Buck Clayton, Walter Page, you know - what was this?

1937, I think it was around January 17th. Benny Goodman was jiving Joe Jackson because you know in those days you could not be under contract with somebody - yeh, 'Shoeless Joe Jackson,' that's what his name was. The first time that I ever met Mr. Freddie Green . He was down at the Black Cat place, so after we got through playing the recording it was decided that Claude should go back to Kansas City or Oklahoma or somewhere, so that's when Freddie Green joined the band, January 1937, and we were still at the Roseland Ballroom.
You made this recording for John Hammond produced this? Producers?

I'm pretty sure Brunswick. It was Billie Holiday recording date with Benny Goodman, Walter Page, Buck Clayton, Freddie Green , Mr. Teddy Wilson, and myself. That's all that was on that, and Shoeless Joe Jackson, that's what they called him... Benny Goodman.
You don't remember one name of one of the tunes, do you?
I don't have it... I have the records.
